sections.html: Screenshots are evidence. In professional security work, undocumented claims don’t exist. Every screenshot must prove you did the work on your system.

sections.label: Deduction:
sections.html: −2.5% per qualifying screenshot short of 20. Twenty qualifying screenshots from a module’s labs earns full screenshot credit; more than 20 earns nothing extra unless a screenshot is your evidence for a stretch goal. A qualifying screenshot is readable, comes from this module’s labs, shows your abc123 (in the terminal prompt, or in the title bar of the full Kali VM window), and sits inline in the .docx next to the text that references it. Duplicates count once. A documented failure you captured and explained counts. Combined with other documentation deductions, the cap is −100%.

sections.label: Critical: VM Name Visibility
paragraphs: Name your VM <your abc123> and give Kali the same hostname. Your abc123 is the ID you use to log into Canvas (for example, aaa000), not your Banner ID number. It then shows in your terminal prompt (kali㉿aaa000) and in the VM window’s title bar.
When the prompt can’t show it (inside a container’s SSH session, a browser window, a GUI tool), capture the entire Kali VM window so your abc123 is visible in its title bar.
Without your VM name, there’s no way to verify you ran the commands. Screenshots without identification could be copied from anywhere — and occasionally are.

sections.label: Where Each Screenshot Goes
paragraphs: Screenshots go inline, inside the .docx, next to the text that references them. Foundation Lab work (X.1 and X.2) goes in the Runbook, under the entry for the tool that produced it. Client work (X.3) goes in Part II, with the finding, methodology step or appendix item it supports. If a runbook entry needs a client screenshot, point to it by figure number with a cross-reference instead of pasting it twice. A screenshot uploaded as a separate file, attached in Canvas or posted as a Canvas comment is not in the packet and does not count.

sections.label: Filename Convention
paragraphs: All screenshots follow this naming pattern: ##-description.png
sections.tip: Two-digit numbers keep files sorted correctly (01, 02… not 1, 2, 10, 11). This matters when you’re compiling 20+ screenshots into a report.

sections.label: Pro Tip:
sections.html: Screenshot as you go. Don’t try to recreate screenshots after the fact. Take them in real-time as you work. Missing a screenshot means redoing the work — or taking the deduction.
Every screenshot is evidence. Make it count.
